thesis: Range Resources is under a definitive all-stock merger agreement with EQT, announced Oct 26, 2026 (Range 8-K). Each Range share converts into 0.987 EQT shares, EQT holders are expected to own about 73% of the combined company, and closing is targeted for Q1 2027, subject to regulatory clearance and both shareholder votes. Range rose about 5.2% today to $56.37 on 4.2x volume, at its 52-week high, as EQT rose to $56.29. At the exchange ratio that is about $55.56 per Range share, so Range sits roughly 1.5% above the implied value, with no competing bid identified. The stock's path appears tied to EQT's share price rather than to Range's own fundamentals. This run found no scheduled ruling in the company's disclosed legal matters (a 2021 securities class action and royalty class actions) and no restatement.
invalidation: The merger breaks, or a competing bid above the exchange-ratio value emerges.

thesis: Surgery Partners is under a definitive agreement (Oct 26, 2026, 8-K) to be acquired by HealthSpan Partners, an affiliate of Bon Secours Mercy Health, for $23.50 per share in cash, an enterprise value of about $5.7B. Bain Capital affiliates are rolling their stake, and closing is expected in Q1 2027, subject to antitrust and shareholder approvals. At $23.35 the stock sits about 0.6% below the deal price, so upside appears capped while a deal break would expose it to a large drop. The company's proxy materials flag potential deal-related litigation as a risk. A March 2026 law-firm investigation over earlier margin guidance has no filed claim identified, and this run found no restatement or scheduled hearing.

Instacart slipped about 1.4% today to $60.055 on 2.6x volume. Reports relayed by Reuters say DoorDash is in advanced talks to buy it for roughly $17B, possibly as early as Oct 28, with talks with Uber no longer active. Sources caution that an agreement is not guaranteed, the company has not confirmed terms, and a combination would face antitrust scrutiny, so the outcome is unresolved. The FTC has an open civil investigative demand over the company's AI pricing tool with no scheduled next step identified; it follows a $60M Instacart+ settlement in Dec 2025. A February 2026 law-firm fiduciary-duty investigation has no filed claim, and this run found no restatement.
invalidation: A signed, company-announced agreement with disclosed terms and a credible regulatory path.

thesis: Centene reported Q3 2026 this morning (8-K). Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.58, against a consensus near $0.07-0.10, and management raised full-year 2026 guidance to adjusted EPS above $5.20 (from above $4.80) and GAAP EPS above $3.46. Medicare Advantage is now expected to break even in 2026, a year ahead of the turnaround plan. The stock traded 2.8x volume and closed up about 1.0% at $68.73, about 5% below its 52-week high. The strongest counter-case is Medicaid margins: the quarter's health benefits ratio was 93.6%, the company reported a GAAP loss of $0.14 per share that this run could not attribute to a specific charge, and management said in July that Medicaid membership declines and acuity shifts would slow margin recovery through 2027. That counter-case is not resolved by today's report, which caps this at medium. A securities class action (Lunstrum v. Centene, S.D.N.Y.) has a lead plaintiff appointed but no scheduled ruling identified, and this run found no restatement.
invalidation: Medicaid cost trends worsen enough to put the raised guidance at risk, or the stock closes back below its pre-report level (~$68.03).

thesis: Noble fell about 5.3% today to $45.27 on 2.3x volume after reporting Q3 2026 on Oct 26. The results were mixed. On the negative side, it posted an adjusted loss of $0.57 per share against expectations of a profit, revenue fell about 8.7% year over year to $729M, and it narrowed full-year revenue and EBITDA guidance while raising capital spending. Offsetting that, revenue came in slightly above estimates, $560M of new contract awards lifted the backlog to $6.7B, and the $0.50 quarterly dividend was maintained. Several law firms announced investigations in August 2026 after the Q2 Brazil rig suspensions, but no filed lawsuit was identified, and this run found no restatement.
invalidation: Q4 results show rigs returning to work at contracted rates with guidance holding, alongside a recovery above the pre-report level (~$47.81).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 19). AVTR edged down about 1.0% to $17.12, about 2% below its 52-week high, and this run found no new company disclosure. The company confirmed it will report Q3 2026 before the open on Oct 28, against a consensus of about $0.21 EPS and $1.62B revenue. The thesis still rests on the Q2 2026 beat and the raised 2026 adjusted EPS guidance. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open: Q3 results tomorrow morning are a pending binary event, and the motion to dismiss the securities class action is still being briefed with no ruling date. This stays medium.
invalidation: Q3 results on Oct 28 miss or guidance is cut, an adverse class-action ruling, or a close back below the 20-day average.

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 20). CLF rebounded about 3.8% today to $13.895, above the ~$12.12 pre-report level, and this run found no new company disclosure. The thesis rests on the Oct 19 Q3 report: adjusted EBITDA of $612M against $575M guidance, Q4 guided to about $715M, and 2027 guided above $4B. Earlier in 2026 the company also announced a $1B Middletown Works optimization project with the cost shared equally with the Department of Energy. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open. The outlook depends on contract changes and steel-price forecasts, and the Hamilton (Stelco) layoffs confirmed Oct 21 point to tariff pressure on the Canadian unit. This stays medium.
invalidation: Steel prices or contract pricing weaken enough to put the Q4/2027 EBITDA outlook at risk, a confirmed material Stelco shutdown or forced sale, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$12.12).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 22). ROIV rose about 1.4% to $36.565, above its ~$34.92 pre-announcement level, and this run found no new company disclosure. The thesis rests on the Oct 21 CLARITY Phase 3 results for brepocitinib in non-infectious uveitis. The company had already filed a new drug application for dermatomyositis (disclosed Feb 2026) and has Phase 3 work under way in cutaneous sarcoidosis. The counter-case named in the prior thesis remains open: the uveitis sNDA is not planned until 1H 2027, so approval for this indication and its commercial weight are still pending. Fiscal Q2 results on Nov 9 are the next scheduled event. This stays medium.
invalidation: Full CLARITY data or FDA feedback reveal a safety or efficacy problem, or a close back below the pre-announcement level (~$34.92).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 26). RNG eased about 0.8% to $85.64, and this run found no new company disclosure. The thesis rests on the Oct 22 Q3 2026 report (8-K). Revenue rose 5.9% to $676M, above the $664-670M guidance, and the non-GAAP operating margin reached 24.7%, up about 190bp. Full-year guidance was raised to $2.650-2.657B in revenue, $5.07-5.12 in non-GAAP EPS and $620-630M in free cash flow. ARR from customers using a paid AI product doubled to nearly 15% of the total. The strongest counter-case is competitive: growth is only about 6% in a crowded cloud-communications market. That doesn't change the read, because the beat, the margin expansion and the raised EPS and free-cash-flow guidance all come from the company's own disclosed results at that growth rate. This is the counter-case named and resolved in the prior thesis, and no new fact reopens it. A January 2026 law-firm investigation notice has no filed claim, the 10-Q shows no material proceeding, and the next earnings report is about four months away (Feb 2027).
invalidation: Q4 revenue or margin falls short of the raised guidance, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$79.42).
